extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and third-party requesters preparing ex parte reexamination requests before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and filing ex parte reexamination requests under 35 U.S.C. 302–304 with the USPTO, including what must be shown to raise a substantial new question of patentability and how to present cited prior art and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 304, the Office must determine whether 'a substantial new question of patentability' affecting any claim has been raised; 37 CFR 1.510(b)(1) requires a request to include 'a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must clearly set forth in detail what the requester considers the SNQ to be in view of patents and printed publications and must point out how the questions raised are substantially different from those raised previously in examination. If such a new question is found, reexamination will be ordered. KSR's clarification of obviousness does not alter the SNQ legal standard — simply asking the Office to reexamine previously-applied art based only on KSR (without presenting the art in a new light) will not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: New/non-cumulative technological teaching requirement for relied-upon references
rubrics_metrics.description: For a request under 35 U.S.C. 302, it is not sufficient to propose rejections — it must be demonstrated that a patent or printed publication relied upon 'presents a new, non-cumulative technological teaching that was not previously considered and discussed on the record' during relevant prior examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester must show the reference offers a technological teaching not previously considered on the prosecution record (including other prior proceedings). Mere restatement of previously considered teachings without new analysis will not establish an SNQ. See MPEP § 2242 for further implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art may raise SNQ only if presented in a new light
rubrics_metrics.description: After the 2002 Act, an SNQ can be raised by patents/printed publications 'previously cited by or to the Office' only if the old art is 'presented/viewed in a new light, or in a different way, as compared with its use in the earlier examination(s), in view of a material new argument or interpretation presented in the request.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests relying on previously applied prior art must present a material new analysis or interpretation (including rationales authorized by KSR) to demonstrate why the earlier consideration was inadequate or why the art now raises new questions about patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on permissible grounds in a 35 U.S.C. 302 request
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions in a reexamination request under 35 U.S.C. 302 must be based on patents or printed publications; questions relating to grounds other than prior art patents/printed publications should not be included and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of matters not to include: public use, on sale, conduct by parties, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, 35 U.S.C. 112, insufficiency of disclosure, etc. A patent/printed publication cannot be used merely as evidence of an alleged public use or on-sale activity; it must be applied directly to claims under 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement applying prior art — pertinency and manner to each claim
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 302 and 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2) require the request to include 'an identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested, and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed by patent owner, the request may also point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art. The prior art applied must reflect the appropriate prior art regime (first-inventor-to-file vs. first-to-invent) that governed the original examination and the statement must be consistent with that regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of the explanation; claim-chart/limitation-by-limitation comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere citation of new patents/printed publications without explanation does not comply with 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2). The requester must explain how each cited reference or combination is applied to all claims the requester considers to merit reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally provide a detailed claim chart comparing limitation-by-limitation each claim with the relevant teachings of each reference (see sample request in MPEP § 2214). For proposed obviousness rejections, provide at least one basis for combining references and a statement why the claims would have been obvious over the combination. Preferably quote pertinent teachings with page/column/line/figure citations. The MPEP contains explicit examples of inappropriate language (e.g., lumping claims or alternative combinations) and appropriate language showing precise, claim-by-claim formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of appropriate vs inappropriate claim-language formulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP gives specific examples of inappropriate and appropriate language when asserting anticipation or obviousness against claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inappropriate examples include lumping multiple alternative rejections together (e.g., 'Claim 1 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 102 as being anticipated by, or in the alternative, under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith'), or listing multiple alternatives without separate explanations. Appropriate examples are claim-specific statements (e.g., 'Claim 1 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 102 as being anticipated by Smith.' or 'Claim 2 is unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over Smith in view of Jones.'). Use clear, separate explanations for each claim and each combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of inadequate explanation; Notice of Failure to Comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Any failure to provide the required explanation for a document, combination, or claim will be identified in a 'Notice of Failure to Comply with Ex Parte Reexamination Request Filing Requirements' (see MPEP § 2227).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a notice is received the requester may either (A) provide a separate explanation for each identified combination/document/claim, or (B) explicitly withdraw any document, combination, or claim for which there is no explanation. Withdrawn items then require no further explanation; acceptance of an otherwise defective request is possible if the request is still readily understood from what was provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations/other written evidence may be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations or other written evidence which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination (see MPEP § 2258).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence can be used to clarify or establish dates/contents of references, subject to applicable rules on admissibility and weight; consult MPEP § 2258 for handling during reexamination/examination stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions — limited role in establishing SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration under 35 U.S.C. 303 of an ex parte reexamination request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 is limited to patents and printed publications. An admission per se may not be the basis for establishing an SNQ of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the patent file or court record may be used in conjunction with patents/printed publications to determine scope and content of prior art; a third party may not submit admissions made by the patent owner outside the file unless entered into a court record. Admissions entered from court records and filed in reexamination may be admitted but will not be given weight as an admission to establish an SNQ on their own. Admissions must stand on their own; supplemental information further defining the admission would be improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of prior art required; legibility and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(3) requires a copy of each patent or printed publication relied on or referred to in the request. If the copy is not legible or its scanned image will not be legible, it is deemed not provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color photographs and similar color submissions, if legible, are retained as artifacts. Non-English documents require an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts; an English summary or abstract is usually insufficient. There is a waiver for submission of copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications (per 37 CFR 1.98) unless specifically required by the Office. Failure to provide a required copy or legible copy will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting copies of copending reexamination proceedings/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required nor permitted to submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (which could be mistaken for a new request/filing); instead provide the application/proceeding number and status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not permitted may be returned, expunged or discarded at the Office’s discretion. Where relevance of a parent application is material, notify the Office of the parent application number and its status rather than submitting full copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) requires requesters to include a copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested to serve as the specification for the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full copy of the printed patent (double-column format including the front page), and include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, reexamination certificate, federal court decisions, complaints in pending civil actions, or interference/derivation decisions so that a complete patent history is before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Service for third-party requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is a person other than the patent owner, the owner must be served with a copy of the request in its entirety at the correspondence address indicated in 37 CFR 1.33(c). The certificate of service must set forth the name/address of the party served and the method of service and must be attached to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy served on the patent owner must include a copy of the certificate of service. If service was not possible after reasonable efforts, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office with a cover letter explaining the efforts made and why service was unsuccessful. Use of clear wording such as 'Duplicate Copy of Request Filed under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(5) When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible' is strongly encouraged to avoid duplicate filing fee issues. See MPEP § 2266.03 for additional service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments included in a patent owner’s request
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.510(e), a patent owner may include a proposed amendment with a reexamination request, but any such amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)–(j) and MPEP § 2250 as to format and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment adds claims, excess claims fees per 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. The decision on whether to order reexamination is based on the wording of the patent claims in effect at the time of the request (i.e., proposed amendments are ignored for the order decision). If reexamination is ordered, subsequent prosecution will be on the basis of claims as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and who receives Office communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner(s) in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the correspondence address in the patent file (37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owner(s) or their registered attorney/agent of record, or by a registered practitioner acting under 37 CFR 1.34. To have correspondence sent to a different attorney or agent, a new power of attorney must be filed (see MPEP §§ 324 or 325). Practitioners have duties under 37 CFR 11.104 to inform clients/former clients of significant correspondence; double correspondence by the Office is not normally undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing address, mail stop labeling, and permitted transmission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Original requests and subsequent reexamination correspondence mailed to the USPTO should be addressed to the appropriate Mail Stop (e.g., 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' — Central Reexamination Unit). Requests for ex parte reexamination may not be sent by facsimile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hand-carried or delivery-service papers should be addressed to the Customer Service Window with 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' included. Place Mail Stop information prominently on the first page. Although requests cannot be faxed, subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence may be faxed to Central Reexamination Unit (571) 273-9900. The certificate of mailing, certificate of transmission, and Priority Mail Express® procedures may be used to file papers in a reexamination proceeding except for an original request or corrected/replacement initial request. The USPTO patent electronic filing system accepts requests and proper follow-on papers; consult the Legal Framework for Patent Electronic System for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney or agent from representation
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw from a patent and/or reexamination proceeding, the practitioner must, pursuant to 37 CFR 11.116, certify that they have: (1) given reasonable notice to the client prior to the expiration of the response period that they intend to withdraw; (2) delivered to the client all papers and property to which the client is entitled; and (3) notified the client of any responses that may be due and the time frame for response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Reasonable notice' should allow sufficient time for the client to obtain new counsel before deadline expiration. The practitioner’s responsibility to a former client is not eliminated by withdrawing. A sample form for withdrawal is provided in the MPEP.
